edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. Cant. Liber I 6

source_text: Nigra sum sed formosa, filiae Hierusalem, sicut tabernacula Cedar, sicut pelles Salomonis. Nigra propter paenitentiam et certamina in corpore; formosa propter imaginem Dei et conversionem. Tabernacula Cedar nigra sunt; pelles Salomonis ornatae. Ne videatis me quod fusca sim, quia decoloravit me sol: tentationum sol aliquando animam adurit, sed non aufert pulchritudinem interiorem.
pass_a_gloss: Black I-am but beautiful, daughters of-Jerusalem, as tents of-Kedar, as curtains of-Solomon. Black on-account-of penitence and struggles in body; beautiful on-account-of image of-God and conversion...
pass_b_english: [[I am black but beautiful, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:5]]. Black because of penitence and struggles in the body; beautiful because of the image of God and conversion. The tents of Kedar are black; Solomon’s curtains are adorned. [[Do not look at me because I am dark, for the sun has discolored me >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:6]]: the sun of trials sometimes scorches the soul, but does not take away inner beauty.
